why: A moved more real traffic in the migration itself (seed drop plus the dated-snapshot map that unblocks the hard-coded reviewer at four sites) and paired it with the more disciplined system review: every ROUTER.md lever walked, fourteen ranked items, correct exclusions stated (no Router state/background/Files API), and a self-discrediting note that its own 7-of-9 static count overstates what routes at runtime. B has the single sharpest Router insight — Flex plus a smaller reviewer model for a measured 82% per-call drop, on a pipeline where every call is background — but it declines two levers that clearly apply here (fallbacks, provider_timeout) and leaves the app's most-used OpenAI path unrouted pending a decision, so its coverage is narrower even though it built more branches.
A_best: Measured, correctly-diagnosed blockers (24/24 OpenAI requests held by seed=0; gpt-4o-2024-05-13 absent from both catalog and Router's own dated-equivalents table) fixed in policy on the Router-bound copy only, so provider fallback stays byte-identical — plus the m8/m9 notes that discredit its own tooling's optimistic count and flag four divergent runtime copies, and a cache measurement showing gpt-4o-mini didn't cache at all without prompt_cache_key.
B_best: Flex-tier thinking applied to the right call: routing the hard-coded reviewer to gpt-5.4-mini on Flex for a measured 82% cheaper call, offered as a branch mutually exclusive with the conservative same-family gpt-4o option — i.e. it questions whether that stage needs a big model at all — and it hooks aider's LiteLLM traffic (the pipeline's largest token consumer) in the migration itself rather than on a branch.
A_worst: Its own built set leaves Flex entirely unused (correctly noted as blocked on a model change, but then not pursued as a primary path), aider routing sits on a branch rather than in the migration, and the outside check marks four sites 'verified' that A itself proved cannot route (Claude TypeError, DeepSeek/Gemini vendor hosts) — a gap A predicted but could not make the tooling reflect.
B_worst: It deliberately drops Router fallbacks and provider_timeout on a long-running background pipeline where a mid-run failure costs a whole idea — the provenance objection is answerable by recording the served model, not by declining the lever — and it leaves the hard-coded reviewer (~22 calls per paper, four call sites) off Router in the migration even though the price-identical gpt-4o mapping was available.
